skill.hypothesis: Phenomenon: short-horizon reversal embedded within medium-horizon overextension and stress; Measurement object: persistent state of directional overextension penalized by contemporaneous volatility/range stress and partially offset by prior drawdown depth; Persistence hypothesis: in csi500-like cross-sections, stretched winners with elevated path stress mean-revert over the next several days, while already-deep losers have weaker additional downside due to recovery pressure.
skill.grammar: Construct a reversal-state score by combining (i) medium-horizon signed return level as the core state measure, (ii) short-horizon confirmation/exhaustion via recent mean return or rank, (iii) path-stress amplifiers using range/volatility covariance or range level, and (iv) recovery offset using lower-tail drawdown proxies such as min_ret1_20 or delay_ret5_1. Template: negative trend-state measure + negative recent extension measure + positive stress measure + positive drawdown/recovery measure.
skill.applicability: Most applicable in liquid small/mid-cap cross-sections when medium-horizon dispersion is high and recent moves appear overextended rather than fundamentally repriced; less applicable during strong one-way trend regimes with broad market beta dominance.
